messages:
oncall-bot: Paging @sam — latency SLO alerts firing (p99 > 1.5s) for router-ingress in us-west-2, multiple customers seeing streaming stalls :rotating_light:
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0314-72 — severity P1 — paging oncall
sam: on it, joining bridge. I'm fresh on call, what's the immediate impact?
mika: p99 is spiking to ~2.8s on text generation, p95 elevated too. Streaming stalls show long tail frames stuck on LB handoff for certain shard ids. Customer error rate still low but UX degraded for heavy streaming sessions.
ashley: we're seeing a routing policy oscillation between weight-set v2 and fallback v2.1 on the LB. Some shards get 80% of traffic. 1 node in shard-usw2-7 is saturated w/ NVMe IO and GPU queueing, driving tail.
sam: can you paste the policy version and recent deploys?
ashley: last policy deploy: lb-policy-service 2026-03-14T02:12Z -> v2.7.1. Rollout started 1958499000. We see health checks OK but weight assignments flipped repeatedly for the same partition key range.
mika: metrics: p50 120ms, p95 430ms, p99 2.8s for the affected router route. Streaming stalls visible as long-lived chunk ack delays. Link: https://grafana.redwood/streaming/incident/1958501234 (internal)
lia: cs reports 3 paying customers saw visible stalls in product; one opened a support ticket. They reported partial transcript loss until retry.
sam: immediate mitigation options: 1) revert lb-policy v2.7.1 2) pin traffic away from shard-usw2-7 3) force eager-fallback to smaller model variant for affected customers. Thoughts?
devin: pinning traffic is quickest. We can add a temporary routing override that drains shard-usw2-7 and reweights evenly across other shards. I'll prepare the `route-override` patch.
ashley: also we can throttle per-connection prefix batching to reduce KV cache pressure on that node. But that needs careful tuning.
mika: prioritize routing override + revert would be safer; revert may take longer to propagate if CI checks. Sam, want me to start rollback?
sam: yes please start rollback and do pin concurrently. Notify infra when ready for route change. I'll take customer comms.
devin: applying route-override now:```
kubectl -n lb-config apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: route-override-incident-1958501234
data:
  pin_shards: "usw2-7"
  action: drain
  ttl: "1800"
EOF
```
devin: patch applied, pushing to control-plane. Rolling update in progress. Expect changes to take effect in ~30s.
ashley: double-checking router logs for misroute pattern:```
[2026-03-14T04:00:12Z] router.usw2: shard=usw2-7 route_key=customer:1234 -> weight=0.82
[2026-03-14T04:00:42Z] router.usw2: shard=usw2-7 route_key=customer:1234 -> weight=0.05
[2026-03-14T04:01:10Z] router.usw2: shard=usw2-7 route_key=customer:1234 -> weight=0.79
```
ashley: those flips line up with the policy service re-evaluations; looks like race on policy recompute when health-check latency > threshold, fallback loop causes weight thrash.
mika: rollback initiated for lb-policy-service -> reverting to v2.6.9. It's a config-only rollback, less risk.
sam: lia, can you message the affected customers that we're investigating and may do a brief mitigation change? Keep it high level.
lia: on it — message queued: "We're seeing increased tail latency in us-west. Engineers are mitigating; we'll update in 30 minutes."
devin: control-plane shows route override converged, traffic away from shard-usw2-7. I can see p99 dropping in one minute.
mika: p99 now 1.1s and trending down, p95 back to 320ms. Streaming stall count decreased by 78% in last 90s.
sam: excellent. Keep rollback running until we confirm stability for 10 minutes, then we can do a careful canary of a fixed policy.
ashley: next steps for root cause: 1) reproduce policy recompute race in staging with synthetic health-latency jitter 2) add guard to policy evaluator so it won't oscillate weights >X times in 60s 3) add per-shard circuit breaker to avoid over-accumulating KV cache on a single host.
mika: creating follow-up ticket: SRE-2026-441 policy-evaluator-oscillation. Assigning to router-eng + infra.
sam: I'll keep bridge open for 20m and then handoff to mika for postmortem. Great job. :thumbsup:
lia: customers updated, one asked for root cause details; we'll provide once postmortem done.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-0314-72 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Escalation cleared.
mika: recording timeline and adding graph snapshots to the incident. We'll schedule a blameless postmortem and publish RCA by EOD tomorrow.
ashley: quick note: we should also check cross-region routing table for any stale peer entries that could've biased weights during the deploy. I'll add that to the RCA prep.
sam: thanks everyone — handing over to mika for follow-up. Closing live coordination.
mika: taking ownership for RCA and follow-ups, will ping when draft is ready.
